area: Labs: /practice/lab/[labId], lab progress/asset/grading APIs, graders, simulation jobs, and the lab entry points (LabLink, Practice Hub, home, lesson practice, overview). I ran the 15 lab-related vitest files; all 73 tests pass. Cross-cutting findings: (1) Today an anonymous visitor cannot open any of the 23 available labs. Every lab link ends at a NextAuth sign-in page whose only provider always refuses. (2) Removing the auth gate is not enough on the Worker. The page is force-dynamic and reads content/curriculum/labs/** with node:fs at request time, and those files are not in the Worker bundle (OpenNext's own load-manifest patch notes that readFileSync is unsupported in workerd and inlines manifests instead). The content has to move to build time; check this with cf:preview. (3) Graders are pure TypeScript with zero imports, so they can run in the browser. Simulation can't: it needs a sandbox, a database row and a secret queue token. (4) No test covers the anonymous lessons-only behaviour. playwright.config.ts forces every flag on and every lab spec signs in with AUTH_TEST_MODE and DATABASE_URL. tests/e2e/labs.spec.ts is stale: it expects the old basics-1 v1 title and hint. Nothing unit-tests LabClientPage.

entryPoints: src/lib/auth.ts (authOptions, requireSession, AuthenticationError, placeholder provider, top-level secret check)

features.todayAnonymous: Every (learning) page (all lessons, /curriculum, /practice) mounts next-auth's SessionProvider. It requests GET /api/auth/session on mount and again each time the tab becomes visible (refetchOnWindowFocus defaults to true). The answer is {}, so status is 'unauthenticated' and useAuth().user is always null. Each of those requests is a dynamic Worker call; the runbook measures 100-500 ms CPU when cold. The site has no sign-in button anywhere. requireSession() throws AuthenticationError before touching Prisma. Visiting /api/auth/signin shows NextAuth's default page with a single 'Sign in with Placeholder' button, and it always fails with a CredentialsSignin error.
features.dataShape: Reads only the session JWT: {user:{id (token.sub), name, email}}. Once a session exists, requireSession upserts a User row {id, email, name}. Nothing is stored in the browser.
features.noLoginPlan: Make the identity mode explicit. (1) Add a build-time authEnabled value (NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTH_ENABLED, false on the lessons-only deploy) in src/tools/featureFlags.ts or a new src/lib/auth-mode.ts. (2) Turn AuthProvider into a real context. With auth off it is a LocalIdentityProvider giving {mode:'local', user:null, learnerId: a UUID kept in localStorage 'svuvm.learnerId', loading:false, signOut: no-op}. With auth on it wraps SessionProvider and maps the session to {mode:'account', user}. (3) useAuth must read this context, not call useSession directly: outside production next-auth throws '`useSession` must be wrapped in a <SessionProvider />' once the provider is gone. (4) Mount SessionProvider only when authEnabled, which removes the /api/auth/session traffic from the lessons-only deploy. (5) Keep requireSession() and AuthenticationError as the server seam. Later add getOptionalSession() for routes that should serve both modes. (6) Add a LearnerStore interface in src/lib/learner-store with a browser implementation now and a server one later, chosen by mode. Every feature below uses it. When sign-in arrives, a one-time 'import this browser's data' step moves the registered localStorage keys into the account.
tests: tests/security-config.test.ts: secret required; test-credentials only outside production. One case fails on this branch, reproducibly even when run alone: 'throws an error if both secrets are missing in production' resolves instead of rejecting.
tests/components/Navbar.test.tsx, tests/components/AIAssistantWidget.test.tsx and tests/components/TopicPage.test.tsx all mock @/contexts/AuthContext
tests/fixtures/auth.ts: Playwright sign-in via test-credentials; needs AUTH_TEST_MODE and a disposable DATABASE_URL
No test covers useAuth/AuthContext itself or SessionProvider's network behaviour
features.risk: Medium. If SessionProvider is removed before useAuth changes, dev and test builds crash with the next-auth throw, and production silently gets an undefined context. The import-time secret check means every page that becomes local-only should drop its auth.ts and prisma imports, so it can prerender and no longer needs NEXTAUTH_SECRET at runtime.
